# Flows

<!-- generated by tools/validate.py flows --write; do not edit -->

How the skills hand off to each other. The tables are generated from each skill's `neighbours`. The stage table is kept in the validator; it shows the usual order, not the only one.

## The stages

Each stage ends with a `design-review` at the boundary the development plan names. `usability` appears three times on purpose: it starts with the needs, runs formative evaluation during design and summative evaluation at the end, where `validation` uses its results.

| Stage | Skills, in order | Ends with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start | `setup`, `intake`, `development-plan` | `design-review`: Plan review |
| Needs and use | `user-needs`, `usability` (use specification, user interface specification), `risk` | `design-review`: Design input review |
| Requirements and design | `requirements`, `specifications`, `usability` (formative evaluation) | `design-review`: Design review |
| Build and verify | `implement`, `unit-verification`, `verify` | `design-review`: Verification review |
| Validate and release | `usability` (summative), `validation` (design validation), `approve`, `package`, `release` | `design-review`: Release review |
| After release | `maintenance`, `problem-resolution` | `design-review`: Periodic review |

`traceability`, `risk`, `security-diligence` and `configuration-management` run alongside every stage. Post-market work beyond software maintenance sits outside the skills and in your QMS: the PMS plan, the PMS report (class I) or PSUR (class IIa and above), trend reports and PMCF in the EU; medical device reports (21 CFR 803) and corrections and removals (21 CFR 806) in the US; `maintenance` names an owner for each. `problem-resolution` takes any defect back into the chain. `impact` prices any change and sends reclassification triggers back to `intake`.

For existing code: `design-inputs-from-code`, `hazards-from-code`, `soup-from-code` -> `gap-assessment` -> `requirements`.
